 Fort Bend County District Court
 Cause No. 2025-CV-0036
 Maria Juarez, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Oral Deposition of Maria Juarez
Date:
February 3, 2026
Location:
Offices of Gardner & Morris Law Group
Examining attorney:
Stephanie Williams, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defending attorney:
Garrett Wallace, Gardner & Morris Law Group
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record, so I'll just say I'm the plaintiff in this matter.
Q: Understood. Can you describe how the collision happened?
A: I was driving through an intersection in Pearland, Texas. I had a green light, or at least I believed I did. A vehicle coming from
my right entered the intersection and struck the driver's side of my car.
Q: Had you been to that intersection before?
A: Yes, I drive through it several times a week on my way to work.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?
A: Only for a moment. I noticed it as it came into view, but there was no time to react. It was over almost immediately.
Q: What did you do immediately after the collision?
A: I sat for a bit because my arm hurt badly and I was shaken. A bystander came over and asked if I was okay. Then I called the
police and waited for them to arrive.
Q: Did you seek medical treatment that day?
A: Yes. An ambulance took me to the emergency room. They took X-rays and told me my wrist was fractured.
Q: What treatment have you received since then?
A: I had a cast put on first, and then I was referred to an orthopedic specialist. I've had follow-up appointments and physical
therapy sessions. Some weeks were harder than others to keep up with.
Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: Simple things are difficult. I have trouble opening jars, gripping a coffee mug, and buttoning shirts. I'm right-handed, so
writing and typing have been slow and painful. I had to ask a coworker to help me with some tasks at work.
Q: Have you been able to perform your usual activities at home?
A: Not fully. I used to cook most of my family's dinners, and I've had to cut back. My partner has taken on more of the household
chores, and I feel bad about that.
Q: Has your doctor given you an expected recovery timeline?
A: They said it could take several months before I regain full strength and range of motion, and they haven't ruled out additional
therapy.
</page>
